description: Hi! We're excited to join the NASA Space Apps Challenge to learn new things, share ideas, and solve real-world problems. We're Computer Engineering students at Cebu Technological University Main-Campus, and we're interested in space, science, and technology. We look forward to working with our teammates, learning from others, and creating something meaningful together. We're ready to do our best and enjoy this amazing experience!
summary:
AstroQuest is an interactive educational web experience that brings the forgotten history of NASA's space exploration equipment back to life. Inspired by the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling About NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars," our project transforms space exploration history into an engaging, scroll-based storytelling adventure.

Through AstroQuest, users can explore the Moon, Mars, and deep space while discovering the spacecraft, scientific instruments, and other equipment left behind after their missions. It highlights the purpose, contributions, and scientific achievements of these technologies, showing that even equipment no longer in operation remains part of humanity's journey into space.

By combining interactive storytelling, educational content, and web-based animations, AstroQuest makes space science more accessible, engaging, and enjoyable. Our goal is to raise awareness of NASA's space exploration legacy and remind people that every piece of equipment has a story worth remembering.

Every mission leaves a mark. Every piece of equipment has a story. Through AstroQuest, those stories are never forgotten.
details:
AstroQuest is an interactive, web-based educational experience designed to tell the stories of NASA's spacecraft, scientific instruments, and other space exploration equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It works through a scroll-based storytelling interface, allowing users to navigate different sections and discover the history, purpose, contributions, and scientific achievements of these machines. By transforming information about discarded space equipment into an engaging visual journey, AstroQuest makes space exploration history easier and more enjoyable to understand.

The project provides educational benefits by raising awareness of NASA's missions and highlighting the significance of equipment that remains beyond Earth. Rather than viewing these objects as simply abandoned hardware, AstroQuest presents them as important parts of humanity's scientific achievements and exploration history. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space science, promote learning, and help preserve the stories behind these technological milestones for future generations.

AstroQuest was developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. HTML5 was used to structure the website, CSS3 handled the visual design, layouts, and animations, while JavaScript powered the interactive elements and functionality. The project is accessible through a web browser and does not require users to install additional software or applications.

What makes AstroQuest creative is its approach to storytelling. Instead of presenting information through conventional articles or static presentations, it turns learning into a space-themed exploration experience. Its scroll-based navigation guides users through the content, making the discovery of each piece of equipment feel like progressing through a journey across space.

During development, our team considered accessibility, ease of navigation, educational value, visual presentation, and user engagement. We aimed to create an experience that is informative without being overwhelming and visually engaging without distracting from the scientific information.

Ultimately, AstroQuest seeks to remind people that space exploration is not only about the spacecraft that successfully return or the missions that continue operating. It is also about the machines, instruments, and technologies left behind that contributed to our understanding of the universe. Every piece of equipment represents a mission, a discovery, and a story worth remembering.
